pages.text: The Rite of Sanctity is a small-circle ward for keeping unwanted creatures out. Once raised, the circle does not harm them. It repels them. The result is a brief sacred space where beasts and enemies alike find it difficult to cross the boundary and close in on the caster.

Offer a $(item)Feather$() with $(item)Redstone$() on a small ritual circle and keep $(bold)500 altar power$(/) ready. The rite sustains a repulsive ward around the circle once it takes hold.$(br2)If you want the opposite effect, study $(l:circle_magic/rites)Imprisonment$(/l), which turns the same family of craft toward holding creatures within the boundary instead.

pages.title: Practical Use
pages.text: Sanctity is a witch's quick answer to panic, interruption, and crowding. Cast it while preparing a longer working, defending a ritual site, or buying room against hostile wildlife. It is not permanent and it is not a wall, but for a little while it reminds the world to keep its distance.
